Firstly, they take the moment when there is a spike in deaths during a flu season and attempt to compare it with things that kill more constantly and not in spikes. Secondly, you also have to take into context that people are dying at significantly lower rates due to being on lockdown. Because they can't go outside, people aren't dying at work or in car accidents, for example. Just regular deaths are way, way down. When you take that dip and compare it against the flu spike, it looks worse than it is.

Thirdly, there is huge bias in the reporting of this year's flu. The reason Italy has a higher count is because it has a different reporting system in which anyone who dies with the flu died of the flu. The CDC in America has instructed doctors to do the same thing. This sort of dishonest reporting is hugely spiking the number of deaths allegedly of China Flu. Even despite this, though, the 2020 flu still isn't as deadly as the 2017 flu.

Fourthly, it's worth remembering that we don't normally test for the flu. Traditionally, if you died of pneumonia caused by the flu, you died of "viral pneumonia." It's not relevant exactly which virus caused it. This year, we are testing everyone to make sure they have the China Flu and so instead of dying of "viral pneumonia," they are dying of "COVID-19. You'll notice that deaths of pneumonia, heart attacks, old age, diabetes, etc are way down because huge amounts of them are being attributed to the China Flu. It's just an artefact of how we are reporting deaths.
